question:
What of the following is an example of object moving under uniform circular motion?

I. Motion of the Moon

II. Motion of the Earth
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Uniform circular motion** is defined as the motion of an object traveling at a **constant speed** along a **circular path**. While the speed remains the same, the velocity changes because the direction of the object is constantly changing.
 
• **Statement I: Motion of the Moon:** The Moon revolves around the Earth in a nearly **circular orbit**. Because it maintains a relatively **constant orbital speed** while constantly changing its direction to follow the curve of the orbit, it is a primary example of uniform circular motion. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Statement II: Motion of the Earth:** The Earth revolves around the Sun in an **elliptical orbit** that is very close to being a perfect circle. In many physical models and calculations, this **planetary motion** is considered an example of uniform circular motion because the Earth travels at a nearly **uniform speed** throughout its **365.25-day** journey. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
